Prior versus posterior edge probabilities and Bayes factors

Source: R/mcmc_diag.R
edge_bayes_factors.Rd

Compares each edge probability from edge_probs() with the same probability under the prior alone, estimated from a fit with prior_only = TRUE. The prior probability of an edge, or of a difference \(|D| > c\), is set by the MRF and slab/spike or G-Wishart priors and is generally not 0.5, so a posterior probability is only interpretable next to it. The Bayes factor (posterior odds / prior odds) measures how much the data moved each edge.

Usage

edge_bayes_factors(
  fit,
  prior_fit,
  quantity = c("p_struct", "p_exceed", "p_union"),
  c = NULL,
  scale = c("pcor", "precision"),
  pool_edges = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

The fitted model.

prior_fit

A fit of the same model (same method, hyper, groups, p and diff_deltas) with prior_only = TRUE.

quantity

"p_struct" (default), "p_exceed" or "p_union".

c

Threshold for "p_exceed" and "p_union".

scale

Scale of \(x\) or \(D\) for the magnitude quantities.

pool_edges

If TRUE (default), the prior probability is averaged over the edges of each group (or pair). The default priors treat all edges alike, so this removes Monte Carlo noise; use FALSE for edge-specific priors.

Value

A data frame with type, group1, group2, i, j, prior, posterior, bayes_factor and log10_bf.

Details

To keep Bayes factors finite, probabilities are estimated as \((x + 0.5) / (n + 1)\) from \(x\) of \(n\) iterations, which bounds the Bayes factor by about \(2n\) times the prior odds. Not available for mGHS, whose diagonal prior is improper; under its half-Cauchy local scales the shrinkage weight has a Beta(1/2, 1/2) prior and \(P(w > 0.5) = 0.5\).

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 60, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, method = "ssvs",
                     burnin = 100, nsave = 200, save_draws = FALSE, seed = 1)
prior <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, method = "ssvs",
                       burnin = 100, nsave = 200, save_draws = FALSE,
                       seed = 2, prior_only = TRUE)
head(edge_bayes_factors(fit, prior))
#>    type group1 group2 i j     prior posterior bayes_factor   log10_bf
#> 1 group      1     NA 1 2 0.2236667     0.515   3.68258205  0.5661524
#> 2 group      1     NA 1 3 0.2236667     0.415   2.46527463  0.3918653
#> 3 group      1     NA 2 3 0.2236667     0.800  13.74791098  1.1382367
#> 4 group      1     NA 1 4 0.2236667     0.080   0.31024463 -0.5082957
#> 5 group      1     NA 2 4 0.2236667     0.000   0.00865112 -2.0629277
#> 6 group      1     NA 3 4 0.2236667     0.035   0.13446120 -0.8714030
